Kharkiv New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kharkivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the new Jewish cemetery of Kharkiv, which seems to have emerged during the interwar period and is marked on maps from the 1930s. Kharkiv's Jewish presence dates to the early 18th century, though the city lay beyond the Pale of Settlement, permitting only cantonists and merchants to settle officially; in 1882, Kharkiv students founded Bilu, one of the earliest Zionist groups to settle in Palestine, and the city remained a major Zionist center into the 1920s. The Jewish population grew from 775 in 1863 to over 130,000 (16 percent) by 1939; unusually, Kharkiv avoided pogroms during the 1917 revolutions and Civil War. During the Holodomor of 1932–33, homeless children were buried at this cemetery site, and later the NKVD buried its own victims there as well. Following the German occupation in October 1941, around 10,000 Jews were forced into a ghetto that December, with the majority killed at Drobytskyi Yar in January 1942.
